description: Use this when someone asks what is trending or working in a TikTok niche this week, or wants ideas based on what a niche is posting now. Input: a niche or topic in plain words (for example skincare, gym, TikTok Shop finds, personal finance). Returns the stored public posts with the most views from the last 7 days (14 or 30 days, or the wider niche, when there are too few; it says which), each with its opening line, caption, hashtags, views, date and TikTok link, plus counts of the hashtags and opening styles they share. It reads a stored sample that is refreshed weekly: it looks nothing up on TikTok, is not TikTok’s own trending list, and does not predict or promise views.

niche.description: The niche, sub-niche or topic in plain words, for example skincare, gym, TikTok Shop finds or personal finance. Text.

username.description: Optional. A public TikTok username, used only when no niche is given and that account was already read in the last 24 hours: the niche is then taken from its captions. Nothing is looked up on TikTok.

name: get_tiktok_niche_trends

last_collected.description: The day the newest of these posts was stored.

message.description: One or two plain sentences that say what was found or what went wrong.

niche.description: The niche the request was matched to. level sub_niche = a narrow topic; niche = the whole wider niche.

patterns.description: Counted across the stored posts of the window (up to 60): hashtags used by 2 or more posts, how the opening lines start, and first words that repeat. Counts only, nothing is judged.

status.description: ok, or the plain reason there is no result (not_found, private, no_videos, videos_unavailable, not_enough_videos, invalid_input, unknown_niche, niche_needed, no_data, rate_limited, paused, off, busy, unavailable).

top_posts.description: The stored public posts with the most views in the window, highest first, one per creator (up to 5).

url.description: The post’s public TikTok page: cite it as the source.

views.description: null = the post was stored without a view count.

window_days.description: 7, 14 or 30: how far back the posts go. The shortest window with enough stored posts is used.

window_note.description: Which window was used and why. Say this to the person.

title: TikTok trends in a niche this week
